readingCallout: PlayBlue's public evidence of activity clusters at stages **01** (brand access), **04** (brand narrative) and **05** (the store). Stages **03, 06, 07 and 08** are explicitly not built. That is normal for a pre-launch retailer — but the operating spine and the profitability path both run through the stages with the least in place.

stages.title: Brand & supply sourcing
stages.desc: Securing the right to sell, on workable terms ·

body.label: Description
body.text: Brand partnership negotiation, distributor and importer relationships, private-label development, and increasingly domestic manufacturing. Determines landed cost, which determines everything downstream.

body.label: Sub-stages & technologies
items: Brand and distributor contracting — margin, exclusivity, stock allocation
Import, duty and compliance for global brands
Private-label design, sourcing and QA
Domestic manufacturing and sports-goods cluster sourcing
Vendor management, PO and contract tooling

body.label: Current players
items: **Decathlon** — own brands, own supply chain, ~68% locally sourced in 2024 targeting 85%
**Brand principals** — Puma (₹3,274 Cr), Adidas (₹3,114 Cr), Nike (₹1,380 Cr) control their own India distribution
**Vertically integrated challengers** — Technosport owns its fabric technology and manufacturing
**Domestic manufacturers** — SG, Cosco, MRF Sports, Nivia

body.label: Where PlayBlue plays today
body.text: Active, and this is the structural advantage. Satyam Trivedi's institutional network is the most credible route to 100+ partnerships at seed stage. A Brand Partnerships lead is being recruited to formalise the pipeline. No public evidence of private label or manufacturing — which leaves the landed-cost gap against Decathlon unaddressed.

stages.title: Assortment planning & buying
stages.desc: What to stock, how deep, at what price ·

body.label: Description
body.text: Where margin is won or lost in multi-brand retail, and the hardest thing to do well across six categories and 100+ brands at once.

body.label: Sub-stages & technologies
items: Category architecture and space allocation
Range planning and open-to-buy management
Price architecture and margin planning by category
Demand forecasting and size-curve planning
Merchandise planning systems; AI-assisted allocation

body.label: Current players
items: **Decathlon** — controls assortment end to end through own-brand architecture
**Marketplaces** — effectively outsource assortment to seller supply
**Fashion multi-brand operators** — Shoppers Stop, Lifestyle, Reliance Trends bring mature buying discipline from adjacent categories

body.label: Where PlayBlue plays today
body.text: Forming. The Senior Buyer posting reads as though assortment logic is still being set — it explicitly asks for someone who can identify "white spaces nobody's filled yet." Highest-leverage stage for external demand evidence, and the shortest window in which that evidence is still actionable.

stages.title: Catalogue & product data
stages.desc: The structured layer everything digital sits on ·

body.label: Description
body.text: Unglamorous and load-bearing. Search, filtering, sizing, returns and conversion all depend on it.

body.label: Sub-stages & technologies
items: Product information management (PIM) and taxonomy design
Attribute enrichment, imagery, cross-brand sizing normalisation
Digital asset management
Search and filter relevance tuning
Automated attribute extraction and catalogue QA

body.label: Current players
items: **Marketplaces** — mature catalogue infrastructure at very large scale
**Decathlon** — simplified by own-brand control and one consistent taxonomy
**PIM and commerce vendors** — where the technology scouting question sits

body.label: Where PlayBlue plays today
body.text: Not built. The Catalog Manager posting is explicit: no product data, images, specs, sizing or structure exists. Normalising sizing across 100+ brands is genuinely hard and a known conversion killer — and unlike Decathlon, PlayBlue cannot solve it by controlling the brands.

stages.title: Demand generation & community
stages.desc: Reasons to care before reasons to buy ·

body.label: Description
body.text: In sports retail this extends past advertising into events, teams, athletes, clubs and participation programming.

body.label: Sub-stages & technologies
items: Brand and performance marketing; CAC management
Athlete and team associations, sponsorships
Events, runs, clinics, grassroots programming
Content and owned media
CRM, CDP and audience infrastructure

body.label: Current players
items: **Puma** — cricket sponsorships and Bollywood ambassadors took it to No.1 in India
**Adidas** — Indian national cricket team association
**Decathlon** — participation-led, store-attached playing fields, low ad spend
**cultsport / Cult.fit** — community-led demand generation at scale
**Marketplaces** — category budgets a seed-stage entrant cannot match

body.label: Where PlayBlue plays today
body.text: Active and ahead of the rest of the chain — brand narrative and editorial are live before the store is. Founder access to leagues, teams and athletes is real. The open question is whether community is a marketing posture or an operating model with a data layer behind it.

stages.title: Store format & experience
stages.desc: Where the differentiator lives or dies ·

body.label: Description
body.text: Where stores go, how they are laid out, and what happens between walking in and deciding. "Expert guidance" is a floor-plan and staffing decision before it is a marketing claim.

body.label: Sub-stages & technologies
items: Catchment analysis and site selection
Store design, zoning and space productivity
Trial infrastructure — fitting, gait analysis, racquet demo, testing zones
Staff expertise, training and clienteling tools
POS, footfall measurement, in-store analytics

body.label: Current players
items: **Decathlon** — ~130 stores in 55+ cities, expanding to 190 across 90+ cities on a €100M commitment
**Puma** — 570+ stores
**Technosport** — 300 new stores announced on ₹200 Cr
**Brand flagships** — Nike, Adidas in premium metro locations

body.label: Where PlayBlue plays today
body.text: Building. This is where the seed capital goes and where execution risk concentrates. Constrained Grade A supply and 12–22% rent growth on target high streets make site selection a strategic decision, not a property one.

stages.title: Digital commerce & omnichannel
stages.desc: The storefront and the connective tissue ·

body.label: Description
body.text: Online store plus unified inventory, click-and-collect, endless aisle, and a single customer view across store and app.

body.label: Sub-stages & technologies
items: E-commerce platform and mobile app
Unified inventory and order management
Click-and-collect, ship-from-store, endless aisle
Quick-commerce storefront and dark-store orchestration
Personalisation and conversion optimisation

body.label: Current players
items: **Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Ajio** — where online sports and athleisure discovery happens today
**Decathlon** — own platform plus an Ajio partnership extending reach
**Brand D2C** — Nike, Adidas, Puma apps and loyalty programmes
**Quick commerce** — increasingly carrying sports and fitness SKUs

body.label: Where PlayBlue plays today
body.text: Not built. Building this in parallel with three store launches is the most demanding commitment in the plan, and the stage where a seed-stage team is most directly outgunned. Note that even Decathlon treats marketplaces as necessary distribution rather than pure competition.

body.label: Description
body.text: Moving product at a cost the margin can absorb. The delivery promise makes this a strategic commitment rather than a back-office function.

body.label: Sub-stages & technologies
items: Warehousing and inventory positioning
Dark stores or store-as-node fulfilment
Last mile — owned or 3PL
Returns and reverse logistics
WMS, routing and delivery-promise engines

body.label: Current players
items: **Marketplaces** — national fulfilment at scale advantage
**Quick-commerce operators** — dark-store density that is expensive to replicate
**3PL providers** — the realistic route for a new entrant
**Decathlon** — store-backed fulfilment across 55+ cities

body.label: Where PlayBlue plays today
body.text: Not built. Sports goods are bulky, size-variable and carry higher return rates than most categories, which makes a 4-hour promise structurally expensive. Whether customers will pay for it — or even value it — is testable before it is built, and considerably cheaper to test than to discover.

stages.title: Service, returns & loyalty
stages.desc: Everything that determines a second purchase ·

body.label: Description
body.text: In sport this is unusually rich — servicing, restringing, fitting, coaching, clubs — and it is the natural home of the community ambition.

body.label: Sub-stages & technologies
items: Returns, exchanges and warranty
Product servicing — restringing, bike service, shoe fitting, repair
Membership and loyalty design
Community programming and clubs
CDP, retention analytics, lifecycle marketing

body.label: Current players
items: **Decathlon** — in-store workshops and servicing at scale
**Cult.fit** — membership and retention mechanics in adjacent fitness
**Brand programmes** — Nike Membership, adiClub
**Specialist independents** — servicing depth in running, cycling, racquet sports

body.label: Where PlayBlue plays today
body.text: Not built. The 10M-community ambition sits here with no announced membership construct. This is where Jayam Vora's Fitternity and cultpass experience is most directly transferable — and where the tension with the profitability target is sharpest.
